text:
Payment authorization depends on what the system checks when funds move. An approval record establishes a decision; it does not establish that the final transfer is bound to it.

CERT-In’s November 4, 2026 update reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its October 9 advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks. It recommends binding transaction stages and validating payouts against approved records.

My reading is that credentials can permit a payment call without proving that the particular payment was approved. If the interface does not enforce that connection, approval may not constrain execution.

This evidence concerns the described Indian campaign. It does not establish Canadian incidents, frequency, losses, fully autonomous AI attacks or a weakness in every payment system.

I would ask leaders to trace one approved payment to execution: identify the authorized recipient and amount, then verify what requires the final transfer to match those details.
